candidate.name: Dual-perturbation placement instability / inverse-variance alpha (DPI)
candidate.definition:
S(alpha) = the realised instability of the hard placement when BOTH modalities are resampled at their own honest uncertainty. alpha* = argmin. The estimand is the inverse-variance blending weight.

TWO PERTURBATION FAMILIES, both mandatory:
(E) Expression - Multinomial/Poisson resample of the counts per cell and per spot (or Gaussian data fission with the estimated noise sd; gene bootstrap as a fallback), giving C_feature^(b).
(T) Tree - the essential one is GW-REFERENCE SUBSAMPLING, which senses model discrepancy rather than merely reconstruction noise. Draw s^(b) in {0,1}^n at p = 1/2 and compute L^(b)_ij = [(C_T^o2) a^(b)]_i + [(C_S^o2) b]_j - 2 [C_T Gamma^(b) C_S^T]_ij with a^(b) = (a*s^(b))/(a.s^(b)) and Gamma^(b) = (gamma * s^(b)[:,None]) renormalised. Only half the cells voice a tree-based opinion; all are still placed. Where a lineage character matrix exists (eTRACER, PEtracer, or CNV segments), additionally bootstrap its columns and re-infer the tree with the same pipeline, and use the union of the two perturbations.

For each alpha and b = 1..B: solve gamma^(b)(alpha) and take j_i^(b) = argmax_j gamma^(b)_ij (hard placement, so hedging is not rewarded).

V(alpha) = (1/n) sum_i mean_{b<b'} ||x_{j_i^(b)} - x_{j_i^(b')}|| / D_rand,  D_rand = sum_{j,l} b_j b_l ||x_j - x_l||. V is in [0,1] with 1 = chance. alpha* = argmin V.

ROBUST VARIANT (preferred, because the minimum is shallow): compute the two single-modality curves V_E(alpha) (E only) and V_T(alpha) (T only) and solve V_E(alpha*) = V_T(alpha*). For approximately independent perturbations V ~ V_E + V_T and the crossing coincides with argmin V to first order. Report both and require agreement within one grid step; disagreement means the perturbations are correlated and the decomposition is invalid.

Per-clade: V_k over cells of clade k only; coordinate ascent on alpha_k.

COMPLEXITY: B = 10 solves per alpha per configuration; 8 alphas x 10 x 3 configurations (E-only, T-only, both) ~ 240 solves. Character-bootstrap tree inference is negligible beside the solves. Everything else is O(B^2 n) distance arithmetic.
candidate.why_not_monotone:
alpha -> 0: V = V_E(0), the raw sensitivity of the placement to expression measurement noise - large, because a resample moves a cell across territories. V_T(0) = 0.

alpha -> 1: V = V_T(1), and this is NOT zero, which is the whole design. If only expression were perturbed, V would be monotone decreasing with argmin pinned at 1 - the degenerate-stability trap in its purest form - and that variant is retained here as the built-in NEGATIVE CONTROL. Under reference subsampling V_T(1) > 0 for two reasons: the GW alignment's symmetry-breaking is weak (the alignment is a strict optimum only for non-exchangeable clades, and the gaps are swamped by entropic smoothing), so the clade-to-territory assignment can move; and a tree whose metric is an inconsistent predictor of space gives systematically different advice depending on which cells you ask, which is exactly what half-sampling the reference set exposes. V_E(1) = 0.

INTERIOR: V is the instability of a convex blend of two partially independent noisy evidence sources. To second order V(alpha) ~ (1-alpha)^2 s_E^2 + alpha^2 s_T^2 + 2 alpha(1-alpha) rho s_E s_T, minimised at alpha* = (s_E^2 - rho s_E s_T)/(s_E^2 + s_T^2 - 2 rho s_E s_T), strictly interior whenever both s are non-zero and rho < 1. So the interior minimum exists BY CONSTRUCTION and its location is the inverse-variance weight - a named estimand, not the artefact you get from min(increasing, decreasing), where the crossing is set by arbitrary relative scaling. This distinction matters: a min-of-two-monotone-curves criterion always produces an interior optimum and it is always meaningless.

STATED LIMITATION: the inverse-variance weight equals the accuracy-optimal weight only if both sources are unbiased. The tree is a BIASED predictor for dispersed clades - it drags them to one place - so DPI will systematically over-weight the tree exactly where the catalogue says it hurts. GW-reference subsampling partly converts that bias into observable variance (an inconsistent tree-space relationship is reference-set dependent), which is why it is preferred over a pure character bootstrap; on a near-exact tree such as PEtracer's in-situ lineage a character bootstrap alone gives ~0 perturbation and the criterion collapses back to the degenerate case.
candidate.third_modality_kind: none - the lineage character matrix is used only if already present, and the primary tree perturbation needs nothing beyond C_tree itself
candidate.prediction: On the 11 in-band controlled seeds: V(alpha) is U-shaped with an interior argmin in >= 8/11 and mean |argmin V - argmax accuracy| <= 0.15, beating the expression loss (0.210) and matching or beating the CNV anchor (0.150) with no anchor at all. MANDATORY NEGATIVE CONTROL: the E-only variant must give argmin = 1.000 in >= 9/11 seeds; if it does not, the tree term is not stabilising the coupling and the premise behind this whole lens is wrong. SECOND, DISCRIMINATING PREDICTION - because DPI is variance-optimal rather than accuracy-optimal, its per-clade vector should be biased UPWARD for dispersed clades: alpha_k(dispersed) should exceed the oracle 0.095 while alpha_k(compact) tracks the oracle 0.350, giving a per-clade AUC in the 0.55-0.70 band, i.e. better than the 0.558 dispersion plug-in but well short of the 0.964 achieved with a CNV anchor. Observing AUC > 0.85 would mean the bias argument is wrong and the reference-subsampling perturbation is capturing discrepancy more completely than predicted - a good outcome, but one that must be explained. FALSIFIER: V monotone decreasing under the DUAL perturbation in >= 6/11 seeds means the tree-side perturbation is too small; the approach is then dead as stated and only a larger tree perturbation (character bootstrap plus branch-length noise) could revive it.
candidate.novelty: Nothing in the catalogue perturbs the tree side at all. Every failed criterion treats C_tree as a fixed oracle and either scores the coupling against it (BM/OU likelihood, monotone to alpha = 1 in 10/10) or scores expression reconstruction (monotone to alpha = 0 in 11/11). DPI never scores agreement with either object, so it is not a fit criterion and the structural monotonicity argument - which is an argument about agreement criteria - does not reach it. It is also not the failed joint likelihood logL_expr + w logL_BM: that summed two profiled log-likelihoods, both proportional to -0.5 N log sigma^2, whose derivative ratio never crosses in the interior, giving a bang-bang jump from 0.00 to 0.85; here the two terms are bounded, same-unit realised displacements that enter quadratically in alpha, which is what produces a genuine interior stationary point. Not a plug-in, not an anchor, not supervised transfer, and no third assay - so it also escapes the Q18 dilemma that an anchor good enough to select alpha with is better spent as a feature.

review.duplicates: none for the global arm — nothing in the catalogue perturbs the data on either side, and DPI is not a fit criterion, so the Q20 structural argument genuinely does not reach it. The per-clade arm, however, substantially re-enters a catalogued failure: NOTES.md L120-145, "a per-clade preference cannot be read out of a balanced-OT coupling by perturbation... perturbing one clade's parameter necessarily moves every other clade". Half-sampling at p=1/2 changes EVERY clade's reference mass at once, so V_k is the whole system's response, not clade k's — which is verbatim confound #2 at L55-60. Semi-relaxed tau=0.01 mitigates it (baseline artefact 18/27 -> 10/27) but recovery there was still null (r=+0.074, p=0.71).
review.fatal_reason:
The non-monotonicity argument holds, and that is the problem: it holds as an ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY, so it carries no information about where the minimum sits.

(1) The U-shape is manufactured by the parameterisation, not by the data. At alpha=1 the cost contains C_feature with coefficient exactly 0, so an expression resample cannot change gamma: V_E(1)=0 exactly. At alpha=0 the cost contains L_gw with coefficient exactly 0, so V_T(0)=0 exactly. Each perturbation family perturbs only a term whose weight is driven to zero at one endpoint. Therefore V_E decreasing-to-0 and V_T increasing-from-0, a crossing, and an interior argmin of V_E+V_T are GUARANTEED for any dataset, any tree, including a tree of pure noise. The proposal's own indictment applies to itself: "a min-of-two-monotone-curves criterion always produces an interior optimum and it is always meaningless." Naming the estimand does not repair the scaling problem, it renames it.

(2) The minimum's location is a free knob. alpha* = (s_E^2 - rho s_E s_T)/(s_E^2 + s_T^2 - 2 rho s_E s_T) is a monotone function of s_E/s_T, i.e. of the RATIO of two injected perturbation magnitudes. s_E has a defensible scale (multinomial counting noise). s_T does not: p=1/2 reference subsampling is a bagging convention, not a model of any uncertainty in C_tree. Raise p to 0.85 and s_T shrinks and alpha* moves right; drop it to 0.2 and alpha* moves left. Nothing in the proposal anchors p. This is precisely the "arbitrary relative scaling" the proposal condemns elsewhere.

(3) The estimand is provably the wrong target on the decisive dataset. Inverse-variance weighting is optimal for two UNBIASED estimators with calibrated sampling variances. The proposal concedes the tree is biased, then treats it as a bounded correction. On PEtracer it is the entire story. PEtracer's in-situ lineage is near-exact, so the honest tree uncertainty is ~0, so honest inverse-variance says alpha*->1 — where measured accuracy is 0.1639 against a peak of 0.3022 at alpha=0.6. The proposal escapes this only by swapping the honest perturbation for the uncalibrated one. That is a dilemma, not a design: honest uncertainty gives a catastrophically wrong answer, and the substitute gives whatever p you chose. The underlying reason is conceptual — the variance of a measurement of the tree says nothing about the validity of the tree-to-space MODEL, and it is the model, not the measurement, that alpha is weighting.

(4) The "mandatory negative control" cannot fail. It demands argmin V_E = 1.000 in >=9/11 seeds. Since V_E >= 0 and V_E(1) = 0 identically, argmin V_E = 1.0 in 11/11 for any input whatsoever. A control that cannot fail tests nothing, and offering it as the premise check indicates the endpoint zeros were read as empirical facts rather than identities. (Sole exception: if the FGW outer loop is initialised from an expression-derived coupling, V_E(1) is not exactly 0 — but then the criterion inherits the initialisation-dependence the notes already flag as fragile at L303.)

(5) V measures the wrong kind of variance. argmax_j gamma_ij flips when a perturbation exceeds the top-2 gap of a softmax at temperature eps. The notes record that GW's symmetry-breaking gaps are "small and easily swamped by entropic smoothing" (L416), so at high alpha each row is near-flat across a whole territory and the argmax is close to a coin flip among many near-equal spots. V_T(1) will therefore be large for a reason unrelated to tree quality — cost-landscape degeneracy relative to eps — and that inflation pushes alpha* down. Combined with (2), alpha* is largely determined by eps and p. Note the direction: this makes DPI likely to UNDER-select on PEtracer, reproducing for a third time the exact failure mode of the anchor loss (selected 0.1, truth 0.6).

What is genuinely right here: the criterion is honestly computable with no ground truth and no third modality (counts, C_tree, C_space, gamma are all observable), the expression-derived-anchor circularity does not apply, and the GW-reference-subsampling idea does have a real statistical ancestor (m-out-of-n / information-matrix-equality tests for misspecification). That ancestor is the salvageable part — but it is a hypothesis test against a null, and the proposal instead uses it as an uncalibrated variance in an optimisation. Not fatal for lack of novelty; fatal because the interior optimum it produces is an identity whose location is set by a knob.
review.fixes:
Three of the four defects are repairable, but the repair changes the idea into a different one.

1. REMOVE THE KNOB by testing instead of optimising. Do not report argmin of an unanchored blend. For each alpha, compare the observed tree-side subsample dispersion V_T(alpha; p) against the dispersion predicted under a "tree is correctly specified" null — generate the null by parametric bootstrap from the fitted map at that alpha (simulate cell positions from gamma, re-derive, re-subsample at the SAME p). p then cancels between observed and null. Set alpha* = the largest alpha at which the excess discrepancy does not reject. This is a calibrated misspecification test with a null distribution, it discards the inverse-variance estimand (which item 3 above shows is the wrong target anyway), and it is the only version I would spend solves on.

2. COMMON RANDOM NUMBERS across the alpha grid — same B perturbation seeds at every alpha — otherwise V(alpha) is a noisy function of alpha and, on the author's own account that "the minimum is shallow", B=10 (45 pairs) cannot resolve the argmin to within the 0.15 the prediction claims. With CRN the curve is smooth in alpha and B=10 may suffice; without it, B>=30.

3. STOP MEASURING ENTROPIC TIE-FLIPPING. Replace the hard argmax displacement with a top-2-gap-normalised statistic, or report V alongside the mean top-2 gap so degeneracy-driven and evidence-driven instability can be told apart. Otherwise V_T(1) is dominated by GW near-ties, not by tree discrepancy.

4. DROP the per-clade arm until the global arm survives the shuffled-tree control. If attempted at all, perturb ONE clade's reference membership at a time under semi-relaxed tau=0.01, which the notes show makes single-clade perturbation local (L145, L185-191) — never a global p=1/2 half-sample, which reproduces the catalogued confound exactly.

No repair addresses defect (3), the estimand itself. That one requires abandoning inverse-variance.
review.test_spec:
SHUFFLED-TREE + KNOB-SENSITIVITY CONTROL. Two arms sharing solves, ~256 solves total, no new machinery beyond permuting C_tree.

Design: 2 controlled seeds x alpha in {0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.85} x B=8 perturbations with COMMON RANDOM NUMBERS across alpha. Four conditions: (a) V_E only, expression multinomial resample; (b) V_T only, real C_tree, p=0.5; (c) V_T only, real C_tree, p=0.85; (d) V_T only, LEAF-SHUFFLED C_tree (permute rows+cols of C_tree by a random cell permutation — this destroys tree-space concordance while preserving the tree's distance spectrum exactly), p=0.5. Report argmin of V_E+V_T in each condition, plus V_E(0.85), V_T(0.0), and the mean top-2 gap of gamma at each alpha.

Three kill conditions, any one of which ends it:

K1 (primary). On the leaf-shuffled tree the true accuracy optimum is alpha=0 — a shuffled tree can only add isotropic variance (NOTES.md L360-364). If argmin V under condition (d) lands within one grid step of argmin V under condition (b), DPI is reading the geometry of the cost blend rather than tree quality, and it will report a confident interior alpha on a tree that carries no information. DEAD. It survives only if (d) gives alpha* <= 0.1 while (b) gives alpha* in 0.10-0.35.

K2. If |argmin V(p=0.85) - argmin V(p=0.5)| exceeds one grid step, alpha* is a tuning parameter, not an estimate. DEAD as an estimator regardless of how K1 goes.

K3 (free, diagnostic). Confirm V_E(0.85) and V_T(0.0) are zero to solver tolerance. This is expected — it demonstrates the endpoints are algebraic identities, that the proposal's "mandatory negative control" cannot fail, and that the observed U-shape is not evidence of anything. Report it explicitly so the U-shape is never cited as support.

Why this and not the author's own falsifier: the proposed falsifier ("V monotone decreasing under dual perturbation in >=6/11 seeds") is nearly impossible to trigger, because V_T(0)=0 forces V to rise off alpha=0 whenever the tree perturbation moves anything at all. It would pass on garbage. K1 is the test that can actually distinguish signal from identity, and it is cheaper than the 11-seed U-shape sweep. Run K1/K2 before spending anything on per-clade coordinate ascent.

candidate.name: Excess cross-view agreement over a label-permuted tree null
candidate.definition:
Idea: keep the degenerate construction (both views share the tree, so agreement is 1 at alpha=1) and subtract a null in which the tree has the same shape and the same GW magnitude but no true cell-to-lineage correspondence. The degeneracy then cancels exactly at both endpoints.

Same solver, grid and calibration discipline as VDA. Views are GENE HALVES ONLY; the tree is deliberately shared.

Arm T (true tree): gamma^{A,T}, gamma^{B,T} = solve(C_f^(1), D), solve(C_f^(2), D).
Arm P (null): the SAME two gene halves against D^{pi_r}, the patristic matrix with rows and columns permuted by pi_r, a random permutation of cell labels (R=8 draws). Permuting leaf labels preserves the topology, the edge-length spectrum, the row-mean heterogeneity that makes the GW term non-degenerate (|L|/|F| unchanged) and hence the strength of the attractor; it destroys only which cell is which. For the global variant permute ACROSS clades; for the per-clade variant permute only WITHIN clade k.

Agreement statistic (multivariate intraclass concordance of the two views' posterior-mean placements, scale-free and immune to global hedging):
  A(alpha) = 1 - sum_i a_i ||mu^A_i - mu^B_i||^2 / [ sum_i a_i ||mu^A_i - xbar^A||^2 + sum_i a_i ||mu^B_i - xbar^B||^2 ]
A = 1 for perfect agreement, 0 for independent placements of equal dispersion. Note the denominator is essential: without it, two views that both hedge to the tissue centroid would agree trivially.

  S(alpha) = A_T(alpha) - mean_r A_{P,r}(alpha),   alpha_hat = argmax_alpha S.
Per-clade: S_k, with clade-k-internal label permutation, restricting all sums to i in clade k; one null arm scored for every clade at once (permute within every clade simultaneously) keeps the cost at R extra solves rather than K*R.

Complexity: 2 solves (arm T) + 2R solves (arm P) per alpha = 18 at R=8, 144 over the grid; the alpha=0 solve is shared across arms and can be computed once.
candidate.why_not_monotone:
S vanishes at BOTH endpoints by construction, so an interior extremum is forced by Rolle's theorem. This is a stronger structural guarantee than anything in the catalogue.

S(0) = 0 exactly: at alpha=0 the tree does not enter the cost at all, so arm T and arm P solve identical problems and A_T(0) = A_P(0) to machine precision.
S(1) = 0 exactly: at alpha=1 the expression channel does not enter, so within EACH arm the two gene views are identical problems and A_T(1) = A_P(1) = 1. The alpha=1 degeneracy is not avoided, it is cancelled - it happens identically in both arms and subtracts out.

Sign and location in the interior. The tree acts as a shared attractor pulling both gene views toward a common configuration; the strength of that pull depends on alpha and on the tree's shape, both matched between arms. What is NOT matched is whether the attractor points where the truth is. With the true tree, the attractor coincides with the target each gene half independently points at, so the two halves reinforce and converge faster than the mechanical rate; with a permuted tree, the attractor is an arbitrary configuration that fights each half's own signal, giving the mechanical rate only. Hence S > 0 in the interior, and it is maximal at the alpha that best exploits real lineage information.

Crucially this makes S sensitive to tree BIAS, not just tree noise - which is exactly VDA's blind spot. A clade whose tree is spatially uninformative or actively misleading produces the same mechanical agreement in both arms and cancels to zero, so it cannot push argmax S upward. Run both: agreement between them is strong evidence, disagreement localises whether the problem is noise (VDA moves, S does not) or bias (S moves, VDA does not).
candidate.prediction: Construction check that must pass before anything else is believed: |S(0)| < 1e-10 in 11/11 seeds and S(alpha) -> 0 as alpha -> 0.9 in 11/11; argmax S strictly interior in 11/11 by construction. Substantive predictions on the controlled simulator: argmax S in [0.05, 0.50] in >=8/11 seeds; |argmax S - argmax accuracy| smaller than the CNV anchor loss's 0.150 in >=7/11; max_alpha S exceeds 3 sd of its own permutation-to-permutation spread in >=9/11 (i.e. the excess is detectable, not noise). The discriminating test against VDA: in a simulator variant where EVERY clade is made spatially dispersed (tree present and well reconstructed but spatially uninformative), max_alpha S falls below 2 sd of its permutation noise in >=9/11 - the criterion correctly reports 'no usable tree signal, use alpha=0' - while VDA's V_tree stays small and VDA still selects alpha > 0. On PEtracer M3-4, argmax S >= 0.45. Falsifier: S negative or flat across the interior in >=6/11 seeds, which would mean the true tree adds no cross-view coherence beyond a scrambled one and the whole lens is dead.
candidate.novelty: The project already uses shuffled trees, but only as a significance control on ACCURACY (oracle > shuffled > inverted). Here the permuted tree is a matched null for an AGREEMENT statistic between two independently-evidenced maps, and the subtraction is what pins both endpoints to zero - a device that does not exist anywhere in the catalogue and that no reconstruction loss can imitate, because a loss evaluated on a permuted tree is not on the same scale as one evaluated on the true tree. It is not a fit criterion (nothing is predicted), not a plug-in (no static property is read off a single map), not a transfer rule (nothing is fitted elsewhere), and not a composition/marginal statistic (placement of individual cells is compared, which is the joint statistic the PEtracer failure identified as missing). It also sidesteps the tree-split problem entirely: no half-tree is ever built, so it is applicable when only a precomputed C_tree is available.

review.fatal_reason: The non-monotonicity argument survives (rare here), but the criterion fails one level deeper: the permuted-tree subtraction that pins S to zero at both endpoints also removes every term that could LOCATE alpha. Linearize the compromise as mu^v = (1-a)x_e^v + a x_t with x_e^v = m_e + n_v; set V_e=Var(m_e), V_n=Var(n_v), V_t=Var(x_t), c=Cov(m_e,x_t), where c>0 in arm T and c=0 in arm P by construction. The ICC is the shared-variance fraction, so with u=(1-a)^2 V_e + a^2 V_t, x=2a(1-a)c, N=(1-a)^2 V_n: A_T=(u+x)/(u+x+N), A_P=u/(u+N), and S = xN/[(u+x+N)(u+N)] = 2a(1-a)^3 c V_n /[(u+x+N)(u+N)]. Two consequences. (i) The HEIGHT of S is proportional to c, so S is a good label-free detector of "does this tree carry spatial signal" and the all-dispersed discriminating test will likely pass. (ii) The LOCATION of argmax S is essentially independent of c: with V_e=V_t=V_n=1 the peak sits at a~0.43 for c=0.2, ~0.44 for c=0.5, ~0.42 for c=0.9. It is set by the a(1-a)^3 shape and by V_t/V_e, i.e. by the relative SCALING of the GW and feature blocks -- a normalisation convention, not biology. The accuracy optimum is a function of tree error vs expression error, which S never sees except through the scalar c that factors out of the argmax. This is worse than monotone failure: a monotone criterion announces itself at a grid endpoint, whereas this returns a plausible interior number every time, uncorrelated with the target (~0.43 looks like a near-miss against the simulator's 0.10-0.35 and a near-miss from the other side against PEtracer's 0.6). Three aggravating problems: (a) the grid tops out at 0.85 (BM/OU pinned there 10/10) and S(1)=0 is off-grid, so the structural protection lives in the unevaluated tail; (b) arm P is a frustrated non-convex GW problem whose flat multimodal landscape lets the two gene halves land in different local optima, deflating A_P and inflating S for purely numerical reasons, with the inflation growing in alpha and biasing argmax S upward -- needs a same-init/multi-restart control; (c) the per-clade variant is dead as specified, because within-clade label permutation preserves ALL inter-clade patristic distances, which is where essentially all lineage-space signal lives (clades are spatially compact -- the entire premise), so the null retains the signal and S_k -> 0, with tiny permutation groups and an unstable small within-clade ICC denominator on top. Minor: prediction #1 (|S(0)|<1e-10) is a tautology given identical problems and a deterministic solver, so it validates code rather than the idea; and ~3000 solves is not "moderate".
review.duplicates: none (nearest relative: the existing oracle > shuffled > inverted tree control in NOTES lines 212/358/936, which already establishes the height effect this statistic measures, via accuracy rather than agreement)
review.fixes: Two repairs, both of which abandon argmax S. (1) Demote from selector to DETECTOR: report max_a S with its permutation-to-permutation spread as a label-free pre-flight test of whether the tree carries usable spatial signal, gate the alpha machinery on it, and set alpha from the existing 0.2 plateau default. The analysis supports this use and nothing in the catalogue answers that question without ground truth. (2) Convert argmax into MOMENT-MATCHING: do not take a peak. Fit (V_e, V_t, V_n, c) to the two observed curves A_T(a) and A_P(a) -- two full curves, four unknowns, heavily overdetermined -- then compute a* analytically from the fitted variance decomposition. That is calibration rather than argmax, structurally different from everything catalogued, and it uses the curve shape instead of discarding it; its weak point is that recovering the tree's error relative to truth from c alone needs an identifying assumption, which is where a follow-up proposal should aim. Mandatory regardless: extend the alpha grid to include 1.0; hold solver init and seed identical across arms with multi-restart checks to rule out the frustrated-landscape confound; withdraw the per-clade claim, or replace within-clade permutation with whole-clade-label swaps (which do destroy inter-clade correspondence) and re-derive the null.
review.test_spec: ZERO-SOLVE PRE-CHECK FIRST (~10 lines of numpy, minutes): evaluate S(a) = 2a(1-a)^3 c V_n /[(u+x+N)(u+N)] with u=(1-a)^2 V_e + a^2 V_t, x=2a(1-a)c, N=(1-a)^2 V_n on a fine alpha grid, for c in {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} crossed with V_t/V_e in {0.25,1,4} and V_n/V_e in {0.25,1,4}. FALSIFIER: if argmax_a S varies by less than 0.05 across c at fixed variance ratios, while shifting substantially with V_t/V_e, then the peak encodes cost normalisation rather than tree quality and the idea is dead before any OT solve. My calculation says this is exactly what happens (peak ~0.42-0.44 for every c at V_e=V_t=V_n=1). IF IT SURVIVES, the one simulator test that matters (~380 solves, an order of magnitude below the proposed protocol): do NOT test "argmax S near argmax accuracy on 11 seeds of one setting" -- a constant ~0.3-0.45 passes that by luck. Test CO-MOVEMENT. Sweep a knob that moves the true optimum (character dropout / tree-reconstruction noise, plus expression noise) over 4 settings whose ground-truth argmax accuracy spans roughly 0.1 to 0.7, times 3 seeds = 12 configs; at each compute S on a 4-point alpha grid that includes 1.0, with R=3 permutations, 2 gene halves, fixed solver init across arms. Statistics: Spearman rho between argmax S and argmax accuracy over the 12 points, and sd(argmax S). PASS requires rho >= 0.6 AND sd(argmax S) >= 0.15. PREDICTED FAILURE: sd(argmax S) < 0.10 while argmax accuracy moves by >= 0.4, rho ~ 0, with max_a S nonetheless correlating strongly with tree informativeness -- confirming the height works and the location does not.

candidate.name: Cross-view variance decomposition (VDA)
candidate.definition:
Idea: never score a coupling against a modality. Score two couplings built from DISJOINT HALVES of the same evidence against each other, separately for each channel, and add the two disagreements.

Inputs: X_sc (n x G), X_st (m x G), spot coords x (m x 2), tree graph g with edge-length dict blen, clade indicator omega (n x K). Solver: existing semi-relaxed FGW (spotr/semirelaxed.py::solve_perclade_semirelaxed with perclade_v2.build_perclade_alpha_cost_v2(equalize='measured')), eps=0.02, tau=0.01, T=50, J=3. Grid alpha in {0,.1,.2,.3,.45,.6,.75,.9}.

1. GENE SPLIT. G = G1 (+) G2, random, stratified by mean-expression decile so both halves carry comparable information. Build C_f^(1), C_f^(2) with prepare_ot_inputs on each half.
2. TREE SPLIT. The patristic metric is additive over edges: D_ij = sum_e len(e) * 1[e on path(i,j)]. Partition the edge set E = E1 (+) E2, stratified by node depth, and call prep_petracer.py::patristic(g, root, names, blen_r) with blen_1 = {e: len(e) if e in E1 else 0} and blen_2 likewise. Each D^(r) is itself a valid tree metric (the tree with the other edges contracted). Rescale each to median 1. Preferred variant where a character matrix exists (eTRACER/PEtracer Cassiopeia input): a nonparametric bootstrap over target-site columns with tree re-inference, which is the exact analogue of the gene split; the edge split is the general fallback.
3. For each alpha solve FOUR couplings, each with its OWN sF_ref/sL_ref from make_cladexfgw_scales so the views are internally calibrated (mandatory - an uncalibrated half-tree acts as a lower effective alpha and confounds everything):
   gA = solve(C_f^(1), D_full), gB = solve(C_f^(2), D_full)      [gene-split pair, tree shared]
   gC = solve(C_f^full, D^(1)), gD = solve(C_f^full, D^(2))       [tree-split pair, genes shared]
4. Posterior-mean placement: p^V = row-normalised gamma^V (rows are not constant under semi-relaxed OT), mu^V = p^V @ x, an n x 2 array.
5. V_gene(alpha) = sum_i a_i ||mu^A_i - mu^B_i||^2 / sum_i a_i ;  V_tree(alpha) = same for (C,D). Units: um^2.
6. S(alpha) = [V_gene(alpha) + V_tree(alpha)] / (2 tr Cov(x_spots));  alpha_hat = argmin_alpha S.
7. Average over R=5 independent (gene, edge) splits, held fixed across the alpha grid so the comparison is paired.

Per-clade: restrict the sums in step 5 to i in clade k -> S_k(alpha); deploy by coordinate descent on the vector (alpha_k), 3 sweeps, re-solving with build_perclade_alpha_cost_v2 - i.e. exactly the run_split_half_oracle.py loop with Sec.score replaced by S_k.

Complexity: 4 solves x 8 alphas x 5 splits = 160 semi-relaxed FGW solves (seconds each at PEtracer scale), 2 patristic calls per split, O(nm) per statistic.
candidate.why_not_monotone:
Each component is pinned to EXACTLY ZERO at the endpoint where its own channel is switched off, and is strictly positive at the other end. V_gene(alpha=1) = 0 exactly: C_feature carries weight 0, so the two gene views become bit-identical problems with identical costs (the perclade_v2 equalizer's median|C0| is also identical), hence gamma^A = gamma^B. V_tree(alpha=0) = 0 exactly, by the mirror argument. So S(0) = V_gene(0) > 0 and S(1) = V_tree(1) > 0, and the two curves cross.

Mechanism, in the quadratic caricature mu^V = (1-w)e^V + w t^V with e^V = x* + eps^V (var sigma_e^2 per gene half) and t^V = x* + eta^V (var sigma_t^2 per tree half), the noise being independent ACROSS views in whichever channel was split: V_gene = 2(1-w)^2 sigma_e^2, V_tree = 2 w^2 sigma_t^2, so S is minimised at the strictly interior inverse-variance weight w* = sigma_e^2/(sigma_e^2 + sigma_t^2), with S(w*) = 2 sigma_e^2 sigma_t^2/(sigma_e^2+sigma_t^2) < min(S(0), S(1)). w* is also the MSE-optimal fusion weight when both channels are unbiased, so the argmin coincides with the accuracy optimum in that regime. The degenerate limits are the correct ones: an uninformative tree (sigma_t -> inf) gives w* -> 0, an uninformative expression channel gives w* -> 1.

The alpha=1 degeneracy is confronted directly: it is caused by a channel being COMMON-MODE between views, and V_tree exists precisely to remove that. Splitting genes alone gives a criterion that is monotone to alpha=1 (V_gene alone); splitting the tree alone gives one monotone to alpha=0 (V_tree alone). Only the symmetric pair has an interior optimum, and that is stated as a required ablation, not an assumption.

Why this is not the joint-likelihood trap (logL_expr + w*logL_BM, which jumped 0.00 -> 0.85 with nothing between): the two terms here are in the same physical units (um^2 of placement displacement) and are combined with weight exactly 1 by a variance identity - E||mu^A - mu^B||^2 decomposes additively over independent noise sources - not by a swept hyperparameter. There is no w to choose and no scale mismatch between two -0.5 N log sigma^2 terms.

Known blind spot, stated honestly: splitting the tree exposes tree RECONSTRUCTION noise, not tree BIAS. A clade that is genuinely dispersed in space is dispersed in both tree halves, so its bias is common-mode and invisible to V_tree. VDA therefore estimates the variance-optimal alpha, which upper-bounds the MSE-optimal alpha; expect systematic over-selection in proportion to how much of the tree is spatially misleading. Candidate 'permuted-tree-excess-agreement' is bias-sensitive and is the intended complement.
candidate.prediction: On the controlled simulator (11 in-band seeds, true accuracy optimum 0.10-0.35): (i) component check that must pass first - V_gene monotone DECREASING in alpha in >=10/11 seeds and V_tree monotone INCREASING in >=10/11; if either fails the claimed mechanism is wrong and the criterion should be discarded. (ii) argmin S lies in [0.05, 0.50] in >=9/11 seeds and mean |argmin S - argmax accuracy| <= 0.12, against 0.210 for the expression loss, 0.150 for the CNV anchor loss and ~0.65 for BM logL. (iii) Required ablation: sharing the tree between views (gene split only) moves argmin to the 0.9 grid endpoint in >=9/11 seeds; sharing the genes (tree split only) moves it to 0.0 in >=9/11. (iv) Directional bias prediction: mean(argmin S) - mean(argmax accuracy) > 0, and the gap widens monotonically as the simulator's fraction of dispersed clades is raised from 0 to 1. (v) Negative control: with a leaf-shuffled tree, argmin S -> 0.0 in >=9/11. On PEtracer M3-4, argmin S should land in [0.45, 0.75] (accuracy peaks at 0.60) rather than at 0.10 where the exact-composition anchor loss landed.
candidate.novelty: Not in the catalogue and not reachable by the monotonicity argument. Every catalogued criterion is a functional of ONE coupling scored against a modality (expression loss, held-out genes, BM/OU tree logL, composition/CNV anchor loss) or a plug-in read off a single alpha=0 map. This is a functional of a PAIR of couplings solved from disjoint halves of the same evidence; nothing is reconstructed and no modality is scored, so 'expression-agreement criteria peak at 0, tree-agreement criteria peak at 1' does not apply - the object being measured is the sampling variability of the estimator. Specifically distinct from held-out genes (Q13), where the held-out half is reconstructed FROM one map and is monotone to 0; here the held-out gene half builds a SECOND map and only map-vs-map displacement is scored. Distinct from the plug-in dispersion estimator (Q14) which reads a static property off one alpha=0 map. Distinct from the supervised-transfer route because nothing is transferred and alpha is estimated in situ, which also makes it automatically region-specific - the property the clade x region result says alpha_k actually has.

review.duplicates: none for the global criterion; the per-clade variant S_k is substantively Q14 (plug-in dispersion off a single map) with extra steps — see fatal_reason (F3)
review.fatal_reason:
The non-monotonicity argument SURVIVES — I verified it in the code, and it is the only part of this proposal that does. In `perclade_v2.build_perclade_alpha_cost_v2`, `C0 = (1-alpha_row)*F_hat + alpha_row*L_hat`, and the `equalize="measured"` scale `s_k = target/median|C0|` is measured from C0 itself. At alpha=1 the feature term is multiplied by exactly 0, so C is bit-identical across gene halves and gA==gB (V_gene(1)=0). At alpha=0 the L term is multiplied by exactly 0, so C is bit-identical across tree halves and gC==gD (V_tree(0)=0), even though sL_ref differs between D^(1) and D^(2). Both endpoint claims are literally true. The candidate dies anyway, on four other grounds.

F1 — THE INTERIOR MINIMUM IS PREDICTED BY A CONTENT-FREE ARTEFACT, so prediction (ii) is not diagnostic. Unlike `spotr.build_fgw_cost` (which ends with `s = Z/den` to hold |C| fixed across alpha), `build_perclade_alpha_cost_v2` has NO across-alpha equalizer — its only rescaling is `s_k = clip(target/m_k, 0.5, 2.0)`, which re-centres clades on their own median and therefore leaves the GLOBAL magnitude of C free to vary with alpha. With F_hat and L_hat each normalised to median|·|=1 by `mad_abs`/`make_cladexfgw_scales` and roughly uncorrelated, median|C0| ≈ sqrt((1-a)^2 + a^2): 1.0 at both endpoints, 0.707 at alpha=0.5. A ~29% dip. And eps is fixed at 0.02 with C of order 1, so C/eps ~ 50, deep inside the `exp_smooth_clipped(x, M=40) = exp(40 tanh(x/40))` saturation. A 29% change in cost magnitude at that sharpness is an enormous change in plan diffuseness. Now the statistic: mu^V = p^V @ x is a posterior MEAN. As rows diffuse, every mu_i shrinks toward the global spot centroid and ||mu^A_i - mu^B_i||^2 collapses MECHANICALLY, with no reference to accuracy. So S(alpha) = V_gene + V_tree is guaranteed to dip near mid-grid whether or not the claimed inverse-variance mechanism exists. Normalising by tr Cov(x_spots) is a constant and does not touch this. Worse, the stated ablations pass under the artefact too: gene-split-only still runs to V_gene(1)=0 at the top of the grid, tree-split-only still runs to V_tree(0)=0 at the bottom. The entire falsification plan in (i)-(iii) is satisfied by a criterion carrying zero information.

F2 — IT ESTIMATES THE WRONG NOISE, and the simulator is built so that the right one is invisible. This is admitted as a "blind spot" but it is the whole mechanism, not a corner case. In `simulate_perclade.py` the tree is the exact Cassiopeia birth-death tree — there is NO character matrix and NO reconstruction noise (so the "preferred" target-site bootstrap variant cannot even be run on the named benchmark, and on an exact tree would give sigma_t=0 → w*=1 → alpha_hat at the grid top). What sets the optimal alpha there is the SPACE-side knob: for lambda=0 clades the within-clade spatial deviation is replaced by iid noise (`xy_mix[ii] = cen + sqrt(lam)*dev + sqrt(1-lam)*noise`), the clade centroid preserved. The tree is byte-for-byte unchanged between a lambda=0 and a lambda=1 clade. So the quantity that determines alpha is entirely a tree-vs-space CONCORDANCE (a bias term), and V_tree — the disagreement between two halves of an identical tree — has the same expected magnitude in both groups. VDA is structurally blind to the only signal the simulator encodes. The same holds on PEtracer: its tree is read in situ and confidently, so sigma_t is small, yet accuracy peaks at 0.6 for reasons of partial clade-space coupling, not tree uncertainty.

F3 — THE FREE WEIGHT WAS NOT ELIMINATED, IT WAS HIDDEN IN THE SPLIT DESIGN. The defence against the joint-likelihood trap is "no w to choose; weight exactly 1 by a variance identity". But the identity fixes the COMBINATION given sigma_e and sigma_t, and w* = sigma_e^2/(sigma_e^2+sigma_t^2) is set entirely by the magnitudes of two perturbations the analyst picks and which are not commensurable. A 50/50 gene split is a genuine subsample of an exchangeable population, so V_gene does estimate 2·Var(half-sample estimator); go to 90/10 and w* moves. The edge split has no estimand at all: the full patristic metric is not a sample of edges, so contracting half of them is a PERTURBATION, not a resampling, and its magnitude is a fabrication. It is also structurally biased in the worst direction — for a leaf pair separated by ~24 edges the two halves each concentrate near D/2 (relative sd ~1/sqrt(24)), while for sisters (path of 2 edges) one half is often exactly 0. Median-1 rescaling cannot repair that. So V_tree is dominated by fine within-clade structure and near-blind to deep structure, and D^(1) acquires zero-distance ties between non-identical leaves. w* is therefore a function of an arbitrary design choice, which is a strictly worse position than the swept w of the joint likelihood — there at least the sensitivity was visible.

F4 — THE PER-CLADE VARIANT COLLAPSES INTO Q14. Restricting the sums to clade k makes S_k a measure of how much clade k's plan moves under perturbation, which at fixed alpha is dominated by how diffuse/unpinned that clade's plan already is. That is the Q14 failure verbatim ("a compact clade CONFUSED by expression looks dispersed", AUC 0.558; bimodality version AUC 0.366, inverted). Given F2, expect per-clade AUC ~0.5.

Secondary, non-fatal: at gamma0 = a b^T the GW term is exactly rank-one after double-centering (`compute_Lgw`'s marginal terms are pure row/column offsets, killed by `_dc_rect`, leaving -2·dc(C_T (ab^T) C_S^T) = -2·(centred C_T a)(centred C_S b)^T), so with J_alt=3 the high-alpha regime is driven by a single tree-centrality-vs-spatial-peripherality axis that BOTH edge halves preserve by concentration — a further reason V_tree may be small exactly where it is supposed to be large. And the cost is understated: per-clade coordinate descent is 3 sweeps × K × |grid| × 4 solves × R splits (≈8,600 solves at K=18), not 160.
review.fixes:
Three repairs are needed and only the first two are cheap; even all three leave F2 standing, which is why I still score this low.

(1) MAKE IT SCALE-FREE (kills F1). Never compare an absolute um^2 displacement across alphas whose plans have different entropy. Replace S with a within-alpha-normalised form, e.g. S = 1 - [Var_i(mu^A) + Var_i(mu^B) - E||mu^A-mu^B||^2] / [Var_i(mu^A)+Var_i(mu^B)] — an ICC/split-half reliability, invariant to isotropic shrinkage of the mu cloud. In parallel, hold the entropic temperature fixed: either add the missing across-alpha equalizer (`s = Z/den` as in `build_fgw_cost`) to the perclade_v2 path, or set eps(alpha) ∝ median|C0(alpha)|. Report mean row-entropy of gamma per alpha alongside S in every run so the artefact is visible.

(2) GIVE THE TREE PERTURBATION AN ESTIMAND (blunts F3). Drop the edge split. Where a character matrix exists, bootstrap target-site columns with tree re-inference. Where it does not, do not fabricate one — and critically, CALIBRATE the two perturbations against each other rather than assuming 50/50-vs-50/50 is fair: sweep the gene split fraction and check that argmin S is stable. If argmin S moves with the split fraction, the criterion is reporting the split design, not the data, and should be abandoned.

(3) SWITCH THE PERTURBED CHANNEL TO SPACE (the only route at F2). The quantity that actually sets alpha is tree-vs-space concordance, which lives on the spot side. A perturbation of the SPATIAL metric (spot subsampling, coordinate jitter at the spot-spacing scale, or holding out spatial neighbourhoods) is not common-mode with the tree bias and could in principle expose a clade whose tree drags its plan somewhere space does not support. That is a different candidate, not a patch, and it would need its own endpoint analysis (note that a spatial perturbation affects BOTH channels, so the clean V(0)=0 / V(1)=0 structure is lost).

Not worth doing: the "permuted-tree-excess-agreement" complement named in the proposal cannot rescue this one, because a leaf-shuffled tree changes the tree's spatial informativeness AND its self-consistency at once, so it cannot separate bias from variance either.
review.test_spec:
Two experiments, run in this order. The first is nearly free and kills the criterion as specified; the second is the decisive one and is cheap.

TEST A — the shrinkage prerequisite (zero new FGW solves beyond one alpha sweep; can reuse an existing sweep). For one simulator seed, for each alpha in {0,.1,.2,.3,.45,.6,.75,.9}, solve ONE coupling with the exact specified settings (solve_perclade_semirelaxed + build_perclade_alpha_cost_v2(equalize='measured'), eps=0.02, tau=0.01, T=50, J=3) and record three scalars: (a) median|C0(alpha)| before the s_k rescale, (b) mean row entropy of gamma, (c) the spread of the posterior means, Sp(alpha) = mean_i ||mu_i - mean_j(mu_j)||^2 with mu = rownorm(gamma) @ x. PREDICTION THAT KILLS IT: median|C0| and Sp both have an interior MINIMUM in the grid (I expect near alpha 0.3-0.6, from median|C0| ~ sqrt((1-a)^2+a^2)). If Sp dips by more than ~20% relative to its endpoint values, then S = V_gene + V_tree — which is O(Sp) by construction — is guaranteed an interior minimum at roughly that alpha with no information content, predictions (i)-(iii) of the proposal all pass vacuously, and VDA as written is dead. Only if Sp is flat to within a few percent across the grid does the criterion deserve any of the 160 solves. This costs 8 solves.

TEST B — the informativeness contrast (the decisive kill; ~128 solves, seconds each). simulate_perclade.py already exposes the per-clade lambda knob that sets the tree's spatial informativeness WITHOUT touching the tree (`xy_mix[ii] = cen + sqrt(lam)*dev + sqrt(1-lam)*noise`). Generate two datasets from the SAME seed and the SAME tree: LAM1 with lams=1.0 for every clade (tree maximally spatially informative; true optimal alpha high) and LAM0 with lams=0.0 for every clade (within-clade position is iid noise; tree carries only clade centroids, true optimal alpha low). Confirm the true accuracy optima differ by running the ordinary alpha sweep on each. Then compute S(alpha) on each with R=2 splits (2 datasets × 8 alphas × 4 solves × 2 splits = 128 solves). PREDICTION THAT KILLS IT: argmin S is the same, within one grid step, on LAM0 and LAM1, while argmax accuracy differs by at least two grid steps. Because the trees are identical and only space changed, any criterion built from tree-half disagreement has no channel through which to see the difference except second-order plan effects — so a null result here is the direct confirmation of F2, and a pass would be genuinely surprising and would be the strongest evidence the idea could produce. Report |argmin S - argmax acc| separately for the two configurations; the proposal's own directional prediction (iv) says the gap must widen from LAM1 to LAM0, so this test also checks the one place the author claims to know the criterion fails.

candidate.name: Spot-routed co-location rank contrast: a within-clade pair U-statistic that is sharpness-free
candidate.definition:
From the coupling, the implied cell-cell co-location kernel

  W = (gamma D_b^{-1/2}) (gamma D_b^{-1/2})^T,   W[i,i'] = sum_j gamma[i,j] gamma[i',j] / b_j

W is quadratic in gamma and is NOT a function of gamma^T A, so it lives outside the composition null space.

From the anchor, build a per-cell posterior over spots that is ROUTED THROUGH SPOT PROFILES:

  p[i,j] ∝ b_j * exp( -|| y_i - Y_j ||^2 / (2 sigma^2) ),  normalised over j
  E[i,i'] = sum_j p[i,j] p[i',j] / b_j

with sigma set from the anchor's own replicate/bin noise. Then

  S3(alpha) = Kendall tau (or subsampled AUC) between W and E over WITHIN-CLADE pairs only, i.e. pairs with k_i = k_{i'}

Restricting to within-clade pairs quotients out the clade marginal exactly: all such pairs carry identical clade-level evidence, so S3 is a pure within-clade joint statistic. Rank-based, therefore invariant to any monotone rescaling of gamma's rows -- it inherits S1's immunity to the hedging bias without needing the argmax.

Complexity: exact O(n^2 m) via two matmuls (n=2281, m=429 -> ~2e9 flops, seconds in JAX); or subsample 1e6 within-clade pairs and evaluate columnwise, O(1e6 * m).

Per-clade: tau_k computed on clade k's within-clade pairs gives alpha_k directly.
candidate.why_not_monotone:
alpha -> 0: expression confusion determines which individual cells co-locate; within a clade expression carries almost no discriminating information, so W is effectively arbitrary at the within-clade scale and tau ~ 0.

alpha -> 1: GW co-locates tree-close cells, and the anchor is tree-predicted, so a naive relational statistic would be MAXIMISED here -- that is precisely the Q20 BM/OU failure. The escape is the routing. E is built from the distance between cell i's anchor profile and SPOT j's measured anchor profile, so E carries absolute position. A globally misregistered GW coupling co-locates the right pairs in the wrong places, i.e. in spots whose measured anchor profiles do not support them, so W and E disagree and tau falls. This gives the design rule that generalises beyond this candidate: any co-location or pairwise anchor evidence must be routed through absolute spot-side measurements, never through cell-cell anchor similarity, or it degenerates into the tree-agreement criterion that is monotone to alpha = 1. The candidate ships with the degenerate version as a paired negative control.

So: low at both ends, and both ends fall for mechanistically distinct and separately testable reasons.
candidate.third_modality_kind: Same as S2 -- a sub-clade-resolved anchor measured on both sides, with per-cell profiles on the dissociated side and per-spot profiles on the spatial side. Because S3 is a RANK statistic over ~1e6 pairs, it tolerates much heavier per-bin noise than a reconstruction loss: it needs the ordering of E to be right on average, not its values. Rough requirement: anchor signal-to-noise sufficient that corr(true co-location, E) > 0.1, which at 1e6 pairs is detectable at overwhelming significance. It does NOT need spot composition to be deconvolvable at all, so it survives regimes where S1's Chat is unusable.
candidate.prediction: On the modified simulator (heritable cell-level anchor GP over C_tree, BM layout along the cell tree -- same two changes S2 requires): argmax S3 within 0.10 of the accuracy optimum in >= 7/10 in-band seeds, and S3 strictly interior (not at 0.0 or 0.9) in >= 9/10. Two paired controls that test the mechanism rather than the outcome: (i) rebuild E from cell-cell anchor similarity instead of spot-routed posteriors -- prediction: S3 becomes monotone increasing with argmax at the grid endpoint in >= 8/10 seeds, reproducing the Q20 BM failure on demand and confirming that routing is what buys the interior optimum; (ii) coarsen the composition anchor to K=3 groups -- prediction: S1's argmax degrades but S3's does not move by more than one grid step, because S3 never uses composition. FALSIFIED if (i) does not reproduce the monotone failure, which would mean the routing argument is wrong and some other mechanism is producing the interior optimum.
candidate.novelty: No pairwise, co-location, or rank statistic appears anywhere in the catalogue -- grep for 'colocat', 'pairwise', 'U-statistic', 'contrastive', 'stabilit' in NOTES.md returns nothing relevant. All anchor criteria to date are first-order per-spot reconstructions. It is also distinct from the Q14 plug-in estimators, which computed a per-clade summary (dispersion, bimodality) from a single alpha=0 map and were confounded because a compact-but-confused clade looks dispersed: S3 never summarises a clade's spatial footprint, it compares a pair-level ordering against an independently measured pair-level ordering at every alpha, so 'confused' shows up as disagreement rather than as apparent dispersion.

review.fatal_reason:
Three independent kills, any one sufficient.

(1) THE STATISTIC IS BLIND TO THE ERROR IT CLAIMS TO DETECT. W[i,i'] = sum_j g[i,j]g[i',j]/b_j is a cell x cell contraction of the coupling, hence EXACTLY invariant under any permutation P of spot labels among spots with equal b_j: W(gP) = W(g). E is also a cell x cell object. So a coupling and its spot-permuted version score identically under S3 while placement accuracy differs by the entire range down to the random floor. The candidate's escape argument is "a globally misregistered GW coupling co-locates the right pairs in the wrong places, so W and E disagree" -- but W does not know about places at all; it is a partition-of-cells statistic. GW's gauge freedom is exactly near-isometric spot relabeling, and its only tie-breaker is the (1-alpha)C_feature term, whose weight goes to zero as alpha -> 1. So the criterion's null space is not merely large, it is ALIGNED WITH AND GROWS WITH the specific pathology of large alpha. This is strictly worse than the PEtracer composition failure: there the null space (couplings sharing a composition) was alpha-independent; here it expands with alpha.

(2) THE ROUTING MECHANISM IS ANALYTICALLY FALSE, and this is provable in three lines with no experiment. Using ||y_i - Y||^2 + ||y_i' - Y||^2 = 2||Y - m||^2 + (1/2)||y_i - y_i'||^2 with m = (y_i + y_i')/2:

  E[i,i'] = (1/(Z_i Z_i')) * exp(-||y_i - y_i'||^2 / (4 sigma^2)) * sum_j b_j exp(-||Y_j - m||^2 / sigma^2)

The leading factor IS a Gaussian kernel on cell-cell anchor similarity -- i.e. E is, to leading order, exactly the candidate's own paired negative control (i). Routing through spot profiles contributes one scalar density factor, and that density is over spot profiles in ANCHOR space, not physical space, so it carries no absolute-position information whatsoever. The claim "E carries absolute position" is wrong. Consequence: the candidate REQUIRES a heritable anchor (its simulator plan is a GP over C_tree), so E is a monotone-decreasing function of tree distance; W at alpha -> 1 is monotone-decreasing in tree distance by construction of the GW term; therefore tau(W,E) is maximised at alpha = 1. This is Q20's BM/OU tree-agreement failure re-derived, and control (i) is not a distinct mechanism but the same statistic modulated by a scalar.

(3) REGIME DILEMMA ON THE THIRD MODALITY -- it duplicates one catalogued failure or the other, with no gap in between. If the anchor is DISCRETE (every real anchor in this project: barcodes, CNV, clone calls), then y_i depends only on the group g(i) and E is block-constant on (g,g'). The block mean of W over pairs (i in g, i' in g') equals (1/|g||g'|) sum_j C[g,j] C[g',j] / b_j where C = gamma^T A_g is exactly the composition matrix at the anchor's resolution. So the statistic's signal collapses onto composition at a finer partition -- the PEtracer failure, refined. The claim "S3 never uses composition" is true only for the CLADE-level A and false at the anchor's own resolution. Escaping requires a cell-individual, continuous, sub-clade-resolving anchor measured on BOTH sides. On PEtracer such an anchor is per-cell lineage barcode, i.e. essentially the ground-truth spot assignment, so a pass there is degenerate; on CNV/allelic data it does not exist (copy number is clonal and constant within a clade); the mtDNA-heteroplasmy case is not measurable per cell in situ. The simulator modification (heritable cell-level anchor GP) constructs precisely the one regime no real dataset occupies, which is the project's recurring failure pattern (Q15 CNV anchor worked in sim, Q26 inferCNV died on real data, PEtracer exact anchor died anyway).

ADDITIONAL, non-fatal but disqualifying for the proposed test: "rank-based, therefore invariant to any monotone rescaling of gamma's rows" is false. Scaling row i by c_i scales W's row i, which reorders pairs ACROSS rows; only a global monotone transform of W leaves Kendall tau invariant. Coupling entropy drifts systematically with alpha (blurrier rows at high alpha under entropic regularisation), so W's magnitude structure varies with alpha and can manufacture an interior optimum for reasons unrelated to the claimed mechanism. Even a PASSING simulator run would therefore not confirm the stated mechanism.

Also note the Q18/Q19 crossover objection, which the user's ban on the feature route suspends but does not answer: an anchor with within-clade pair-level resolution is a better map than SpOTr (Q18: expr+anchor 0.617 vs SpOTr 0.310), and if one has p[i,j] at all, the first-order statistic sum_j gamma[i,j] p[i,j] dominates the pairwise contraction while being strictly more informative (it is not spot-permutation invariant).
review.duplicates: Both, depending on anchor regime: with the heritable continuous anchor it requires, it reduces to the Q20 BM/OU tree-agreement criterion (monotone to the alpha grid endpoint, 10/10); with any discrete/group-structured anchor it reduces to the PEtracer composition-reconstruction failure evaluated at a finer partition (selects alpha=0.1 where accuracy peaks at 0.6). There is no anchor regime in which it is neither.
review.fixes:
The salvageable insight is "joint, not marginal". The unsalvageable step is the cell x cell contraction, which throws away the spot index and with it every error mode GW is prone to. Two concrete repairs, in order of promise:

(A) KEEP THE SPOT INDEX. Drop W and E entirely and score the coupling against the anchor posterior at first order but at CELL resolution (not composition resolution): S(alpha) = (1/n) sum_i sum_j gamma[i,j] log p[i,j], or a per-cell rank agreement between the row gamma[i,.] and the row p[i,.]. This is not spot-permutation invariant, so it actually sees misregistration, and it is a JOINT statistic in exactly the sense PEtracer's composition loss was not -- it constrains which individual cell goes where, not the aggregate proportions. This is genuinely distinct from the catalogued composition failure and is the version worth thinking about. (B) IF A PAIRWISE STATISTIC IS WANTED, break the invariance by keeping a spatial index on at least one side: score triples, e.g. rank-agreement between gamma[i,j]gamma[i',j] and p[i,j]p[i',j] over (i,i',j) with j retained rather than summed. Summing over j is the exact step that creates the null space; not summing preserves it. Cost rises to O(n^2 m) pairs-by-spots but subsampling handles it.

(C) MANDATORY PRECONDITION for either: state the anchor regime explicitly and show that E has nonzero within-clade variance for a REAL anchor, not a simulated GP. If the only anchors with within-clade resolution are the ones that are themselves ground truth (PEtracer barcodes), the criterion has no target dataset regardless of whether it works.

SPOT-PERMUTATION INVARIANCE TEST -- no simulator, no refit, minutes of compute, and it is decisive because the predicted result is algebraically forced.

  - recompute soft accuracy: it must fall to approximately the 0.0977 random floor;
  - recompute W = (gamma P) D_b^{-1/2} ((gamma P) D_b^{-1/2})^T and S3 = Kendall tau(W, E) over within-clade pairs, with E built from the section's own per-cell clade profiles.
PREDICTION FROM THE REFUTATION: S3 is numerically IDENTICAL to within floating point (W is exactly invariant under equal-b_j column permutation), while accuracy collapses by ~0.20. A criterion that is constant along a direction in which accuracy varies over its entire range cannot track accuracy, and the demonstration is a proof rather than a statistic, so no seed replication is needed.

SECOND, CHEAPER STILL (5 minutes, pure algebra, no code): verify the identity
  E[i,i'] = (1/(Z_i Z_i')) exp(-||y_i - y_i'||^2 / (4 sigma^2)) sum_j b_j exp(-||Y_j - m||^2 / sigma^2),  m = (y_i + y_i')/2
numerically on random y, Y. If, against expectation, one still wants the simulator run: the informative version is NOT the candidate's. Run S3 and control (i) side by side AND additionally report coupling row entropy vs alpha. If both S3 and control (i) show the same interior optimum and entropy is also non-monotone, the observed optimum is a hedging artefact, not the routing mechanism, and the result is uninformative either way.

candidate.name: Composition-conditional excess: quotient out the marginal, score only what is left
candidate.definition:
For a coupling gamma with realised row masses r_i = sum_j gamma[i,j], clade x spot mass M[j,k] = sum_i gamma[i,j] A[i,k], and clade masses R_k = sum_{i in k} r_i, define the composition-matched maximum-entropy null

  gamma0[i,j] = r_i * M[j, k_i] / R_{k_i}

gamma0 has, by construction, identical column marginals (sum_i gamma0[i,j] = sum_k M[j,k] = b_j), identical row masses, and identical clade x spot mass M. It is the coupling that reproduces the anchor composition while carrying ZERO within-clade information.

With PER-CELL anchor profiles y_i in R^B on the dissociated side and spot anchor profiles Y_j in R^B, define

  D(gamma) = sum_j b_j * || Y_j - sum_i (gamma[i,j]/b_j) * y_i ||^2
  S2(alpha) = ( D(gamma0_alpha) - D(gamma_alpha) ) / D(gamma0_alpha)

S2 is the fraction of the anchor residual explained by within-clade placement, over and above everything the composition explains. Any criterion of this excess form is orthogonal to the composition null space by construction. Complexity O(nmB) per alpha, no extra solves.

Use it as a refinement, not alone: S = S1 + lambda * S2 with lambda set so the two terms have equal interquartile range across the alpha grid; or fix global alpha by S1 and use S2 alone for the per-clade vector. The natural instantiation on PEtracer is a resolution ladder: 'sub-clade' = cutting the tree deeper than the 18 anchor clades, scoring the residual at the finest resolution the anchor supports conditional on the coarsest.
candidate.why_not_monotone:
alpha -> 0: expression confusion operates within clades as strongly as between them (within a clade, cells are transcriptionally near-identical), so the coupling commits to the wrong individual cells and D(gamma) >= D(gamma0). S2 <= 0 at the low end. This is the opposite sign to the composition loss at alpha=0, which is precisely the point: the hedging that MINIMISES the composition MSE is exactly the gamma0 baseline S2 subtracts, so the low-end pull that dragged the MSE optimum down to 0.1 is removed by construction rather than by reweighting.

alpha -> 1: honest weakness, and I state it rather than dress it up. Conditioning on the realised M cancels registration error, which is the very thing that makes the anchor fall at the top end. What remains falling is that within-clade GW is driven by the SHALLOWEST part of the tree, where branch-length estimation error is largest relative to branch length; those commitments are wrong, so the excess declines again. An interior optimum therefore exists iff the within-clade tree is informative but noisier than the within-clade expression signal is confusable -- a condition measurable BEFORE running, by comparing within-clade tree-space Mantel r against within-clade cross-validated expression discriminability. If that comparison fails, S2 abstains rather than misleads.

Because the top end is not structurally guaranteed, S2's job is per-clade alpha_k with global alpha already pinned by S1, where the top-end behaviour is bounded by the global solve.
candidate.third_modality_kind: An anchor with HERITABLE sub-clade resolution: per-cell profiles whose within-clade variation is inherited rather than measurement noise. Allelic CNV at fine segment resolution, mtDNA heteroplasmy (best -- continuous, per-cell, clonal at all depths), somatic SNVs, or in-situ barcodes read at full character resolution. Measurement noise per bin may be large (the statistic aggregates B bins x m spots), but the ratio of heritable within-clade variance to noise variance must exceed roughly 1/sqrt(B * cells_per_spot); at B=150 and 5 cells/spot that is about 0.04, i.e. very permissive. What it cannot tolerate is an anchor whose within-clade variation is pure noise -- then S2 is identically zero.
candidate.prediction:

(2) within-clade positions are drawn iid (Gaussian around cen[k] for compact clades, uniform over the territory for dispersed ones) independently of the within-clade tree structure that C_tree does contain -- so within-clade placement is unidentifiable even with a perfect anchor. (b) MODIFIED simulator, within-clade tree-space Mantel r ~ 0.3: S2 evaluated at the oracle global alpha is significantly positive in >= 9/10 seeds and indistinguishable from 0 at alpha = 0 in >= 9/10. candidate.novelty: Nothing in the catalogue conditions on, or subtracts, a matched null coupling. Every anchor criterion tried (Q15-Q17, Q26, Q27, PEtracer M3-4) scores the composition itself; S2 scores only the orthogonal complement, and does so by explicitly constructing gamma0. It is also not the plug-in estimator of Q14: no per-clade dispersion or bimodality is estimated from an alpha=0 map, and there is no inversion of a mapping-derived statistic. review.duplicates: Not a verbatim duplicate, but a near-neighbour repair of the catalogued anchor-deconvolution-loss family (Q15-Q17, Q26, Q27, PEtracer M3-4 "VAL loss"). The catalogued diagnosis it targets (marginal vs joint) is correct, but the repair shrinks the marginal-joint gap by one resolution level rather than closing it: a sub-clade composition is still a marginal.
review.fatal_reason:
Three independent kills, any one sufficient.

(1) THE ALPHA->1 ARGUMENT IS NOT MADE, AND THE STRUCTURE SAYS S2 IS INCREASING. The author concedes "the top end is not structurally guaranteed." It is worse than unguaranteed: the construction deletes the only force that could bend it down. An interior optimum in this problem exists because expression wins at one scale and the tree wins at another. Conditioning on the realised M removes the BETWEEN-clade scale entirely — which is exactly and only where expression contributes (the confusable-pair design, the 0.58 within-pair discrimination dial, the whole accuracy metric). What is left is the within-clade scale, where the author's own alpha->0 argument stipulates expression is uninformative ("cells are transcriptionally near-identical"). In a regime where one of the two evidence sources is stipulated useless, the optimal weight on the other is 1. So S2 should rise monotonically to the grid endpoint, reproducing the BM/OU logL failure (0.85 in 10/10) one level down the tree. The stated counterforce — "shallow branch lengths are noisiest" — argues the within-clade signal is WEAK, not that it DECLINES with alpha; a weak-but-positive signal still gives argmax at alpha=1. Weak signal also makes S2 a small difference of two large numbers, which is a power problem for an 18-entry per-clade vector, not a selection criterion.

(2) THE RATIO NORMALISATION IMPORTS A PUSH TOWARD ALPHA=1, CONTRADICTING "ORTHOGONAL BY CONSTRUCTION". Expanding with y_i = ybar_{k_i} + u_i, v_j = (1/b_j) sum_i gamma[i,j] u_i, e_j = Y_j - ybar_j(gamma0):
  D(gamma0) - D(gamma) = 2 sum_j b_j <e_j, v_j> - sum_j b_j ||v_j||^2.
Only that NUMERATOR is orthogonal to the composition null space. S2 = 1 - D(gamma)/D(gamma0) divides it by D(gamma0), which IS the coarse composition loss — the catalogued failure. Maximising S2 rewards a LARGE denominator, i.e. rewards WORSE composition. PEtracer's own sweep gives D(gamma0)-like VAL loss .0358 / .0350 / .0404 / .0402 / .0385 / .0381 / .0474 / .0593 across alpha 0->0.9: a ~70% rise from the 0.1 minimum to 0.9. S2 therefore inherits a strong upward drift toward alpha=0.9 from the denominator alone, compounding kill (1) instead of mitigating it. The claim that the excess form is orthogonal "by construction" is true of the numerator and false of the quantity actually proposed.

(3) UNTESTABLE AS BUILT, AND THE PROPOSED FIX BUILDS THE ANSWER INTO THE TESTBED. The precondition diagnosis is correct — I verified both lines: `cell_cnv = cnv_clone[lab] + crng.normal(0, cnv_noise, ...)` (within-clade anchor variation is iid noise on disjoint sc/sp populations, hence exactly zero placement information) and the layout loop `xy[rows] = uniform(...) if is_disp[k] else cen[k] + rng.normal(0, compact_sd, ...)` (within-clade positions iid, independent of the `random_ultrametric` within-clade block written into C_tree). So prediction (a), S2 == 0 everywhere, is correct and trivially true; it validates the diagnosis, not the criterion. But the proposed repair — Brownian layout along the full cell tree — is a change that by construction makes higher alpha better at the within-clade scale. Prediction (c) would then be measuring the simulator edit, not S2. It also destroys the compact/dispersed dichotomy that the AUC metric in (c) is defined on (uniform-over-territory vs Gaussian-around-centroid), and invalidates every range check in the file (tree-vs-layout r 0.85 +/- 0.04, compact spread 0.1-0.45, dispersed spread >0.8, pair separation, within-pair discrimination) plus comparability with all 10-11-seed results already in NOTES. "Moderate" cost is wrong; this is a new simulator plus a full recalibration.

SUPPORTING PROBLEM (not independently fatal, but it closes the real-data escape). The anchor requirement is close to self-contradictory. Clades are called AT the anchor's resolution — numbat clone calls ARE the CNV partition — so within-clade anchor variation is, by construction, noise, which the author admits makes S2 identically zero. The ladder rescue requires deliberately coarsening the clade partition below the anchor's native resolution, at which point S2 is just the anchor loss at native resolution decorrelated from a coarsened copy: still a marginal, one level finer. And that level is squeezed from both sides — coarse enough to be estimable means the marginal-joint gap survives; fine enough to approach the joint means ~1-2 cells per sub-clade per spot at PEtracer's 5.13 cells/spot, where combinatorial sampling noise dominates. The stated noise budget (ratio > 1/sqrt(B * cells_per_spot) ~ 0.04) covers per-bin measurement noise only and says nothing about this. Separately, on PEtracer the only anchor with sub-clade resolution is the lineage barcode, which is what C_tree is built from — so a "success" there would largely be re-measuring the soft-accuracy ground truth at finer resolution, i.e. a positive control, not a selection criterion.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: the precondition finding is real, correctly sourced, and is the most valuable thing in the submission. It should be recorded in NOTES regardless of this verdict, because it means no past experiment could have detected a marginal-vs-joint gap in simulation even if one existed.
