candidate.name: Two-sided split-half stability: perturb the feature channel and the tree channel separately and take the geometric mean of the two reproducibilities
candidate.definition:
Two independent perturbations, one per input channel.
  - Feature channel: split genes into disjoint halves g1, g2, build C_feature^(1), C_feature^(2) with the full tree.
  - Tree channel: split the lineage CHARACTERS into halves (PEtracer target sites, CNV segments, SNV sites), rebuild the tree independently on each half, giving C_tree^(1), C_tree^(2) with the full gene set. If only a fixed C_tree is available, substitute a parametric bootstrap: perturb branch lengths by their estimated standard errors, or run two independent NJ fits on character bootstraps.

At each alpha solve four couplings and form two reproducibilities:
  A_expr(alpha) = agree( gamma(g1, tree_full), gamma(g2, tree_full) )
  A_tree(alpha) = agree( gamma(genes_full, t1), gamma(genes_full, t2) )

Agreement must be joint-sensitive, spatially graded (a near-miss is near-agreement) and sharpness-invariant:
  q_i = gamma[i,:] / sum_j gamma[i,j];  K_s = exp( -C_space^2 / (2 h^2) ), h = median nearest-neighbour spot distance
  agree(gamma, gamma') = (1/n) sum_i  (q_i^T K_s q'_i) / sqrt( (q_i^T K_s q_i)(q'_i^T K_s q'_i) )
This is a normalised spatial cross-correlation in [0,1], unchanged by rescaling either row.

  S5(alpha) = sqrt( A_expr(alpha) * A_tree(alpha) )     (also report min, which is more conservative)

Average over R random splits (R = 5). Per-clade: restrict the average over i to clade k, giving A_expr,k and A_tree,k and hence alpha_k. Cost 4R solves per alpha, ~160 solves for an 8-point grid at R=5.
candidate.why_not_monotone:
The two ends are pinned analytically and in OPPOSITE directions, which is the whole construction.

alpha = 1: the feature cost enters with weight (1 - alpha) = 0, so the two gene halves give identical couplings and A_expr(1) = 1 EXACTLY. Meanwhile GW alone is a quadratic assignment with many near-optimal, mutually inconsistent solutions, so two independently estimated half-trees give different answers and A_tree(1) = c1 < 1. S5(1) = sqrt(c1).

alpha = 0: the tree enters with weight 0, so A_tree(0) = 1 EXACTLY. Meanwhile in the confusable regime expression cannot separate clades, near-ties abound, and two gene halves resolve them differently, so A_expr(0) = c0 < 1. S5(0) = sqrt(c0).

Interior maximum exists iff A_expr rises before A_tree falls. There is a mechanism for that gap, and it is the same one that drives candidate 4: a TINY alpha suffices to break near-ties, because the tree term only has to exceed the expression cost DIFFERENCE between competing spots, which is ~0 in the confusable regime; whereas destabilising the solution requires the tree term to exceed the expression cost LEVEL, which is O(1). The window between 'breaks ties' and 'overrides evidence' is precisely the accuracy plateau the project measured at [0.10, 0.35]. Candidate 4 is the cheap deterministic reading of that window; candidate 5 is the expensive stochastic reading, and their agreement is itself evidence.

Unlike candidate 4 the interior optimum is NOT structurally guaranteed -- if both transitions happen at the same alpha, S5 is monotone and the criterion abstains. But this is the only candidate that measures the RELIABILITY of the solution rather than its fit, so it is the one least exposed to the Q20 theorem, which is a statement about fit criteria.
candidate.prediction: Mechanism check first, worth running on its own: A_expr(alpha) increasing and A_tree(alpha) decreasing over the grid in >= 9/10 in-band seeds of the controlled simulator, with A_expr(1) = 1 and A_tree(0) = 1 to solver tolerance. Then: argmax S5 within 0.15 of the accuracy optimum in >= 7/10 seeds, and S5 strictly interior in >= 8/10. On PEtracer, where the tree channel splits naturally by lineage target site: argmax S5 = 0.60 +/- one grid step on M3-4 and 0.20 +/- one step on M3-1/M3-2. Per-clade on PEtracer: the S5 vector beats uniform-at-same-mean on held-out spots in >= 6/9 of the existing split-half splits. Sharpest falsification: if A_expr and A_tree turn over at the SAME alpha, S5 has no interior maximum and the 'tie-breaking precedes overriding' mechanism is wrong -- which would also predict candidate 4's elbow to be absent, so the two candidates fail or succeed together and running both is a genuine cross-check rather than two shots at the same target. A second falsifier: A_tree flat to alpha=1, meaning GW is unimodal here and instability is not available as a signal.
candidate.novelty: Nothing in the catalogue perturbs the inputs and measures reproducibility -- there is no bootstrap, resampling, or stability criterion anywhere in NOTES.md; the only split-half in the project is of SPOTS, used to measure held-out headroom of an oracle alpha vector, not to select alpha. It is structurally outside the Q20 result, which is a statement about criteria measuring agreement with expression or agreement with the tree: S5 measures agreement of a solution with ITSELF under resampling of its own inputs, and its two endpoint values are set by two different failure modes (expression near-ties, GW multimodality) rather than by two opposed fit terms whose derivative ratio never crosses. It is also not the Q13 held-out-gene test: that split genes to check overfitting of a reconstruction loss and found it equally monotone; here the gene split is a perturbation whose effect is measured on the COUPLING, and the tree channel is perturbed symmetrically, which Q13 never did.

review.duplicates: none (not a catalogued duplicate; the per-clade variant reproduces the q14 plug-in confound, and the S5 = increasing x decreasing form reproduces the Q20 joint-likelihood form)
review.fatal_reason:
The non-monotonicity argument does not survive, and the criterion smuggles in a free parameter that is exactly as unidentifiable as alpha.

(1) LEADING ORDER, log S5 IS LINEAR IN ALPHA. A perturbation of channel c enters the cost with weight w_c(alpha), so the coupling's response scales as w_c(alpha)*sigma_c divided by the assignment margin m(alpha). To first order 1 - A_expr(a) ~ k(1-a)sigma_e/m(a) and 1 - A_tree(a) ~ k*a*sigma_t/m(a), hence 2 log S5(a) ~ -k[(1-a)sigma_e + a*sigma_t]/m(a). With m roughly constant this is LINEAR in alpha with slope proportional to (sigma_e - sigma_t): monotone, argmax at a boundary, sign decided by which channel is noisier. Both endpoint pins (A_expr(1)=1, A_tree(0)=1) are consistent with this null and therefore confirm nothing. The proposal's endpoint analysis establishes only that a decreasing and an increasing function are being multiplied — which is the Q20 joint-likelihood shape (logL_expr + w*logL_BM, swept over 10 weights, no interior optimum in 9/10 seeds), with the weight silently frozen at 1:1 in log space. An interior optimum requires the derivative ratio to cross, i.e. it requires m(alpha) to be concave with an interior peak strong enough to beat the linear numerator. That mechanism is asserted, never argued, and the notes say the relevant cost gaps are "small and easily swamped by entropic smoothing".

(2) THE ARGMAX IS SET BY sigma_e/sigma_t, WHICH IS A KNOB. From the expansion, argmax S5 is tilted away from any margin peak toward whichever channel is perturbed less. sigma_e (half the genes) and sigma_t (half the characters, or branch-length jitter) are incommensurable; nothing makes "half and half" comparable in cost units. So the proposal replaces "choose alpha without ground truth" with "choose the ratio of two perturbation scales without ground truth". Worse for the prespecified test: the controlled simulator HAS NO CHARACTER MATRIX — simulate_controlled.py builds the tree by neighbour-joining on the layout with branch-length noise bisected to a target fidelity — so sigma_t is literally a dial the experimenter sets. Every prediction listed ("argmax within 0.15 in >=7/10") is therefore unfalsifiable: a miss is attributable to mis-set jitter, a hit to a lucky setting.

(3) THE TREE PERTURBATION IS LARGELY ANNIHILATED BY DESIGN. compute_Lgw is followed by _dc_rect double-centering, which the notes record as annihilating additive f(i)+g(j) structure (that is the ROOT CAUSE section: the balanced-tree GW term measured 1.0e-07). Terminal-branch-length jitter adds a constant to every distance involving leaf i — purely additive — so it is a NULL perturbation of the cost. Only topology and internal-branch changes register. Combined with the notes' own correction that "GW is rigid up to global isometry" and that for a generic unbalanced tree the correct alignment is a strict optimum, the expected outcome is A_tree ~ flat near 1, S5 ~ A_expr, monotone increasing, argmax alpha=1. That is the proposal's own falsifier #2, and the project's recorded findings already predict it.

(4) THE AGREEMENT STATISTIC IS NOT SHARPNESS-INVARIANT, AND THE BIAS RUNS WITH ALPHA. Row-rescaling invariance is vacuous (rows are already normalised to sum 1). Under the Gaussian model, two blobs of width w at displacement d give agree = exp(-d^2/(2(h^2+2w^2))): agreement INCREASES with blur at fixed error. Sinkhorn runs at fixed eps and the L_gw term is smooth/low-contrast relative to the noisy high-rank C_feature, so the coupling's effective blur drifts with alpha even though build_fgw_cost holds median|C| roughly constant (s = Z/den). Blur drift biases both A's monotonically and contaminates the very comparison the criterion rests on.

(5) THE ENDPOINT PINS ARE NOT EXACT IN THIS CODEBASE. In build_fgw_cost, s = Z/den with Z = median|F_hat| + median|L_hat(gamma)|. At alpha=0 the cost is F_hat*s and s still depends on the TREE through median|L_hat|, so two half-trees give two different temperatures and A_tree(0) < 1 for pure normalisation reasons. Symmetrically the no_struct flag (mL < 0.001*mF) depends on the gene split. The "analytically pinned in opposite directions" claim is about an idealised objective, not the solver in use.

(6) STABILITY MEASURES DECISIVENESS, NOT CORRECTNESS. The gain mechanism the project documented is POOLING: the GW term makes a clade move together, turning n independent 55/45 decisions into one. Past the optimum the same mechanism drags a dispersed clade to one WRONG territory — a configuration that is maximally stable under gene resampling and, if the tree is well determined, under character resampling too. Nothing in S5 separates confidently-right from confidently-wrong; this is the classic failure of clustering-stability model selection (stability is maximised by the most rigid solution). Per-clade it is worse: A_expr,k at low alpha is essentially a measure of expression confusability of clade k, so alpha_k rises for expression-confusable clades — precisely the confound that killed q14 ("a compact clade CONFUSED by expression looks dispersed", AUC 0.558; bimodality AUC 0.366, inverted). A clade that is both expression-confusable and spatially dispersed wants LOW alpha_k and gets HIGH from S5.

Cost makes this worse: ~160 solves per grid per seed plus tree refits, for a criterion whose leading-order behaviour is a monotone null and whose test on the designated simulator cannot falsify it.
review.fixes:
Not rescuable in the proposed form, but three repairs would be preconditions for anyone revisiting it:

(a) REMOVE THE FREE KNOB. The two perturbations must be calibrated to equal magnitude in the cost's own units. build_fgw_cost already normalises F_hat and L_hat to median|.| = 1, so choose the tree perturbation magnitude such that median|DC(L_hat) - DC(L_hat')| equals median|DC(F_hat) - DC(F_hat')| from the gene split. Without this S5 is a dial, not an estimator. Note this also exposes that terminal-branch jitter is annihilated by DC and cannot be calibrated at all — the perturbation must be topological (character bootstrap + NJ), which the controlled simulator cannot supply, so the mechanism check would have to move to PEtracer target sites from the start.

(b) DE-BIAS THE AGREEMENT. Replace the cosine with a blur-corrected effective displacement: recover each row's own spread from the UN-normalised self term q_i^T K_s q_i and report D_i^2 = -2(h^2 + 2w_i^2) log(agree_i) in microns, or compare hard argmax assignments. Also freeze s to a constant (alpha- and split-independent) so the endpoint pins are exact, and hold the coupling's mean row entropy fixed across alpha by tuning eps per alpha, otherwise blur drift alone sets the argmax.

(c) FACE THE CONFIDENTLY-WRONG PROBLEM. Same-view stability cannot distinguish rigidity from correctness; any repair needs a term that is low when the solution is stable BECAUSE one channel has overridden the other. Note that the obvious move — agreement of gamma(alpha) with an expression-only reference and with a tree-only reference — reproduces the identical increasing-times-decreasing trap and buys nothing.

If (a) and (b) are done, the surviving content is the margin-concavity claim in (1), which is testable for near-zero compute on its own (see test_spec). Test that FIRST; if it fails, the stability construction cannot work and 160 solves are saved.
review.test_spec:
ZERO-SOLVE PRE-TEST (minutes, decisive, no new couplings). The only mechanism that can give S5 an interior optimum is an interior maximum of the assignment margin m(alpha). Measure it directly. For each alpha in the EXISTING controlled-simulator sweep (11 in-band seeds), reload the saved gamma, rebuild C = build_fgw_cost(alpha, ...) with the saved sF_ref/sL_ref, and compute per row i the entropic-scaled margin mu_i(alpha) = (C[i,(2)] - C[i,(1)])/eps, where (1),(2) are the two smallest entries. Record mean_i mu_i and the mean row entropy H_i of gamma. PREDICTION THAT KILLS IT: mean margin is monotone in alpha, or its peak sits at a grid endpoint, in >=8/11 seeds — then no interior optimum of S5 is available and the whole construction is dead. It also directly exposes objection (4): if mean row entropy drifts monotonically with alpha, the agreement statistic is biased by blur before any stability is measured. Only if the margin peaks in [0.10, 0.35] in most seeds is the mechanism live.

CHEAP CONFIRMATORY TEST IF THE PRE-TEST PASSES (18 solves/seed, 3 seeds, not 160). At three alphas only {0.0, 0.20, 1.0}, R=3 splits, compute A_expr and A_tree. Check three things: (i) c1 = A_tree(1). If c1 > 0.95 the GW term is unimodal here (as "rigid up to global isometry" predicts), S5 collapses to the monotone A_expr, dead. (ii) LINEARITY NULL: regress -log A_expr on (1-alpha) and -log A_tree on alpha through the exact endpoints. If both are linear to within split noise, log S5 is linear, argmax is at a boundary, and no R and no finer grid can help — dead. (iii) KNOB TEST, the single sharpest falsifier: rerun with the tree perturbation at 0.5x and 2x its calibrated magnitude. If argmax S5 moves by more than one grid step, the criterion is reporting sigma_e/sigma_t, not alpha, and it is dead regardless of (i) and (ii). Run (iii) even if (i) and (ii) look favourable.
